kf: **Vasculitis** is classified by vessel size: **small** (palpable purpura), **medium** (nodules, livedo racemosa, ulcers), **large** (rarely skin).
Always ask: is it skin-limited or systemic? Check **urine dipstick and BP** in every patient.
Biopsy an early lesion (<48 h) with direct IF; deep biopsy for medium-vessel disease.
Screen: FBC, U&E, LFT, CRP, ANA, ANCA, complement, hepatitis B/C, HIV, cryoglobulins, immunoglobulins.
Same-day: unwell, renal involvement, haemoptysis, neuropathy, gut ischaemia, or child with possible meningococcal disease.
myths: **"Skin vasculitis is just a rash"**: it can be the first sign of kidney or lung disease.
patho_lead: Vasculitis is **inflammation of vessel walls**; the size of vessel decides what you see.

mech.t: Immune complexes in post-capillary venules: palpable purpura, wheals.
mech.cap: Small-vessel vasculitis with neutrophils and red-cell leakage.

mech.t: Arteries at the dermo-subcutaneous junction: nodules, livedo racemosa, ulcers, digital infarcts.
ANCA activate neutrophils against small–medium vessels (GPA, MPA, EGPA).
The same process in kidney, lung, nerve and gut causes organ damage.

comp: Renal failure, pulmonary haemorrhage, neuropathy, gut infarction, ulcers.
prog: Skin-limited forms usually settle; systemic vasculitis needs immunosuppression.
